title: Holi, the festival of colours.
lines: In India there is a very happy festival.
It's the festival of colours, and it's called Holi.
Holi is in spring, when winter is over and the flowers start to bloom again.
This year Arjun is celebrating Holi with his grandma and grandpa in India.
Arjun is six years old.
He lives in Belgium, but now he's on holiday in Grandma's village.
Arjun, says Grandma, tomorrow is Holi.
Then everything gets very colourful!
The evening before Holi the people in the village make a big fire.
They dance around it and they sing.
The fire crackles.
Crackle, crackle.
The fire means: the bad goes away, and the good stays.
The next morning Arjun wakes up early.
He puts on his oldest white T-shirt, because today everything is allowed to get dirty!
Grandma gives him a plate of coloured powder.
Red powder, yellow powder, green powder, blue powder and pink powder.
And she gives him a water pistol.
Holi hai!
shouts Grandpa.
That means: it's Holi!
Arjun goes outside.
All the children of the village are there.
And the grown-ups too.
Everyone throws coloured powder.
Poof!
A cloud of pink.
Poof!
A cloud of yellow.
Arjun rubs green powder on his cousin Rohan's cheek.
Rohan throws blue powder in Arjun's hair.
Hee hee hee!
They squirt their water pistols.
Psssht!
The coloured water splashes everywhere.
After an hour Arjun isn't white anymore.
His T-shirt is red, yellow, green, blue and pink.
His hair is purple.
And his nose is completely orange!
He looks like a rainbow.
Grandma has to laugh.
She can hardly recognise her grandson.
And people dance to the music of the drums.
Dum, dum, tak, dum, dum, tak.
Everyone laughs and hugs each other.
At Holi everyone says sorry if they've had an argument, and then they're friends again.
Then they go inside to eat.
Grandma has made tasty things.
Gujiya, sweet pastries filled with nuts.
And there's cold, sweet milk with almonds.
Mmm!
In the afternoon Arjun has to have a long bath.
The water turns completely purple.
But his nose stays a little orange for three more days.
And when he's back in Belgium, he tells his teacher all about it.
Can we celebrate Holi in class too?
he asks.
And the teacher says yes, but with paint on paper!
